elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: The offending sentence at the second § 12.4 ("During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter, Customer shall not develop, market, sell, or acquire any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory.") is struck and rendered as "12.4 [Reserved.]"; retained § 12.3 affirmatively states "Nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service ... or conducting business in any field or territory," and Vendor acknowledges Customer "has made no exclusivity, non-compete ... commitment." No field-of-use or territory restraint on Customer remains (deterministic check "no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains" ok).

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no restriction survives the redline, so the scoping condition does not apply. With § 12.4 reserved and § 12.3 retained, there is no covenant whose product scope could exceed a single named competing product.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: the 24-month post-term tail was the only temporal reach and it has been deleted; nothing binds Customer either during or after the term.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: with the covenant struck, the duration is zero, which cannot exceed 12 months.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: no restriction remains, and retained § 12.3 expressly confirms nothing restricts Customer from "developing ... any product or service."
Conditional element: no restriction remains, and retained § 12.3 expressly confirms nothing restricts Customer from "acquiring ... any product or service."

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is met by outright deletion of the Customer-side non-compete in the duplicate § 12.4, leaving no field-of-use, product, or territory restraint on Customer anywhere in the rendered language.

Fallback elements are vacuously satisfied because the deletion removes the restriction to which each limitation would attach; the drafter correctly took the stronger preferred position rather than negotiating the narrowed covenant.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only the offending sentence, substitutes a neutral "[Reserved.]" placeholder so the numbering and any cross-references to Article 12 do not dangle, and adds no replacement permission, survival tail, procedure, or other extras. Customer-favourable § 12.3 is retained verbatim, and the non-solicitation/no-hire language in the first § 12.4 is left alone rather than being swept up (which would have been a minimality failure and a double-flag of a different commercial term).
